For the sustainable and secure future of the increasing population, grains, vegetables, fruits, edible oils, pulses, milk, honey and other agricultural products will have to be produced in abundance in the coming times. But the agricultural land available to fulfil these needs is shrinking and most of the inputs for agricultural produce are becoming expensive. On the other hand, the financial condition of the farmer is deteriorating due to the farmer not getting the price of the product as per the cost. Keeping all these problems in mind, the Department of Agronomy, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar has decided to develop one hectare integrated farming system model which is useful in increasing the income of farmers as well as improving the soil health. Under this farming system model dairy, vegetable, horticulture, mushroom cultivation, vermicompost production, biogas etc. have been added along with crops. Farmer families get continuous income from all these agriculture based enterprises. In this way, the farmer family can meet its needs as well as increase its income per hectare per year.

Maize+cowpea-oat-sweet sudan grass: In this fodder based cropping system, sow maize + cowpea mix cropping in between 25 June to 10 July harvest it after 80 to 90 days after sowing when the maize crop is between milk ripe and dough stage of grain development. Sow oat in the first week of October to last week of October. After that in summer season sow sweet sudan grass in the second fortnight of march to second fortnight of April. The first cutting is ready in 45-50 days after sowing. Subsequently, cuttings can be taken after an interval of about 30-35 days.

Green gram-mustard-green gram: In this cropping system grow a short duration variety of green gram in the first fortnight of July. The short duration crop varieties shall vacate the field in the mid of September for timely sowing of succeeding crop of mustard with recommended seed rate and practices. Thereafter, sow summer crop green gram in last week of march to first week of April. This cropping system gives highest net returns with substantial improvement in soil fertility in relation to organic carbon, available N, P and K also improve over time.
